newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Another N.Korean defects, was prisoner - paper.
newsitem.headline: Another N.Korean defects, was prisoner - paper.

text.p: A North Korean seeking asylum arrived at Seoul international airport from Beijing on Sunday, South Korean authorities said, and a newspaper identified the man as a former political prisoner.
Monday's edition of the Chosun Ilbo said Kang Chul-ho contacted South Korean authorities while in transit on a flight from Beijing to Osaka, Japan.
He was travelling under forged Chinese papers as Lee Myung-Ho, 28, the paper said.

Chosun Ilbo, which has a record of exclusives on North Korean defectors, said Kang escaped from North Korea to China in August, 1993. He had served three and a half years in a political prison camp up to 1991.
The man is now being held by the Agency for National Security Planning, South Korea's intelligence organisation, an agency official said.
The official, who declined to be named, confirmed details of the newspaper report but said the defector claimed he left North Korea in October 1992.

Last Thursday a North Korean woman in her 20s fled barefoot and hungry to South Korea through the heavily mined and guarded Demilitarised Zone that has bisected the Korean peninsula since the 1950-53 Korean War.
South Korea is negotiating with China for safe passage to Seoul of North Korea's top ideologue, who defected to a South Korean diplomatic mission in Beijing on February 12.
The Chosun Ilbo said Kang's father was executed in public after an attempted family suicide, and Kang was forced to denounce his father at the execution.

With the help of ethnic Koreans in China he paid 5,000 yuan ($600) for fake travel papers used by merchant seamen and boarded a Korean Air flight bound for Japan, where he had arranged employment, the paper said.
He contacted a Chosun Ilbo reporter and airport security officials in Seoul and was later whisked away by intelligence operatives, the paper said.

South Korean authorities have become wary of revealing personal details of North Korean asylum seekers since a high-profile defector, reportedly once related through marriage to North Korean leader Kim Jong-il, was shot by two gunmen in a Seoul suburb on February 15.

Seoul police have said they believed North Korean hitmen were responsible and the assassination was intended as a warning to ideologue Hwang Jang-yop, now holed-up in Seoul's mission in Beijing, and other would-be defectors.
Nevertheless, the Chosun Ilbo published a picture of Kang wearing a smart jacket and thick sweater.
